title: Source tax tariff: children
purpose: Ask one block of questions per child (no maximum, age judged on the first working day) to decide whether each child counts, whether tariff H applies and what the child digit is.

stories.title: Ask about children only of employees who need a source tax tariff
stories.i_want: to be asked about my children only when a source tax tariff code has to be worked out for me
stories.so_that: I give no personal data about my children that no party needs, while Lonio still has what it needs to compute my tariff code
stories.priority_reason: Data minimisation is a core goal (G-01), and HR said source tax questions should only go to people who are subject to source tax (F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: The children step is shown only after a 'yes' to having children
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is subject to source tax and source tax details are asked (step 6 Source tax details), and the employee answered whether they (or, if married or in a registered partnership, either partner) have biological or adopted children
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues to step 7 Children
acceptance_criteria.then: the child questions are asked only if the answer was 'yes'. With 'no', no child question is asked and the child digit of the tariff code is 0.

Single resident of Germany without children

acceptance_criteria.title: No child questions for employees not subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and is Swiss, or is non-Swiss with a C permit, or is otherwise not subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: neither the question about having children nor any child question is asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents: child questions only with more than 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers the cross-border questions (step 5), which come before denomination, spouse and children
acceptance_criteria.then: the child questions are asked only if the employee does not return daily and expects more than 45 work-related non-return days in the year (and has children). With daily return or at most 45 non-return days, the result is 'in principle no source tax liability' and no child question is asked.

stories.title: One block per child: age status and household
stories.i_want: to describe each of my children in a separate block, starting with whether the child is a minor or an adult in first education and whether the child lives in my household
stories.so_that: every child who may count for my source tax tariff is captured, and children who cannot count need no further answers
stories.priority_reason: Without the per-child answers Lonio cannot compute the child digit of the tariff code, which replaces HR's manual calculator step (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: As many child blocks as the employee needs
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked the child questions (subject to source tax, source tax details asked, and 'yes' to having children)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee fills in step 7 Children
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can add one block per child and remove a block again; there is no maximum number of children (assumption D-044, to be verified by a domain expert). At least one child block is filled in. Every child question in a block is required whenever it is asked. Answers are recorded for HR and used only to compute the source tax tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Age status per child, judged on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee states the child's age status
acceptance_criteria.then: the choices are exactly 'Minor', 'Adult in first education' and 'Neither', and the child's situation on the employee's first working day counts (assumption D-044, to be verified by a domain expert). 'Neither' ends the block: no further question is asked for that child and the child does not count.

acceptance_criteria.title: Same household asked for minors and adults in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: a child block whose age status is 'Minor' or 'Adult in first education'
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues in that block
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether the child lives in their household; the follow-up questions depend on this answer.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child answers that no longer apply are not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee filled in child blocks and then changes an earlier answer so that child questions no longer apply (for example 'no' to having children, or a change that makes them not subject to source tax), or removes a child block
acceptance_criteria.then: the child answers that no longer apply are discarded and not recorded; before submission they are kept so that going back and forth loses no input.

stories.title: Minor child living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: the custody, common household, alternating custody and main-contributor answers for each minor child living in the employee's household
stories.so_that: the child is counted, counted with tariff H or not counted exactly as the Zurich calculator does
stories.priority_reason: A wrong per-child result gives a wrong tariff letter or child digit; Lonio now owns the tariff result (D-001, D-009).

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.given: a child block with age status 'Minor' and 'yes' to living in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues in that block
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must state the parental custody: 'Shared custody' or 'Sole custody'. With shared custody, the employee must answer whether they live in a common household with the child's other parent (yes/no). Without a common household, the employee must answer whether there is alternating custody (yes/no). The main financial contributor ('Myself' or 'Other parent') is asked when there is alternating custody, and for single, divorced, separated or widowed employees who live in a common household with the other parent; married employees and registered partners in a common household are not asked it. For this, Married and Registered partnership form one group and Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated the other, as in the calculator (assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert).

examples.name: Married, sole custody
Married, shared custody, common household: no contributor question
Single, shared custody, common household: contributor asked
Shared custody, no common household: alternating custody asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Per-child result for a minor child in the household
acceptance_criteria.given: a completed block for a minor child living in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the per-child result
acceptance_criteria.then: the result follows the calculator: sole custody counts the child (with tariff H for single, divorced, separated or widowed employees); shared custody with a common household counts the child for married employees and registered partners, and for the other group only if the employee is the main contributor (then with H); without a common household and with alternating custody the child counts only if the employee is the main contributor (with H for the single group); without alternating custody the child does not count for married employees and registered partners and counts with H for the single group. Observed calculator results win over the general rule (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert); results marked inferred are compared with the calculator before go-live (D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage).

stories.title: Minor child not living in the employee's household
stories.i_want: the custody or parental care, alternating custody and main-contributor answers for each minor child who does not live in the employee's household
stories.so_that: such a child counts only in the cases where the Zurich calculator counts it
stories.priority_reason: Counting a child wrongly gives a wrong tariff code; Lonio now owns the tariff result (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for a minor child outside the household
acceptance_criteria.given: a child block with age status 'Minor' and 'no' to living in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues in that block
acceptance_criteria.then: married employees and registered partners must answer whether custody is shared (yes/no); single, divorced, separated and widowed employees must answer whether they have parental care (yes/no) - each group gets only its own question (grouping per assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert). With 'yes', the employee must answer whether there is alternating custody (yes/no), and with alternating custody, who makes the larger financial contribution ('Myself' or 'Other parent'). With 'no', the block ends.

acceptance_criteria.title: Per-child result for a minor child outside the household
acceptance_criteria.given: a completed block for a minor child not living in the employee's household
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the per-child result
acceptance_criteria.then: the child counts only with shared custody (married group) or parental care (single group), alternating custody and the employee as main contributor - counted for married employees and registered partners, counted with tariff H for single, divorced, separated or widowed employees. In every other case the child does not count. Observed calculator results win (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert); inferred results are compared with the calculator before go-live (D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage).

stories.title: Adult child in first education
stories.i_want: the household, common household, main-contributor and maintenance answers for each adult child in first education
stories.so_that: the child counts, counts with tariff H or does not count exactly as the Zurich calculator decides
stories.priority_reason: Adult children in first education change the child digit and can give tariff H; a wrong result gives a wrong tariff code (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Questions for an adult child in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: a child block with age status 'Adult in first education'
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues in that block
acceptance_criteria.then: if the child lives in the household, the employee must answer whether they live in a common household with the child's other parent (yes/no). With a common household, single, divorced, separated and widowed employees must say who makes the larger financial contribution ('Myself' or 'Other parent'); married employees and registered partners are not asked anything more. If the child does not live in the household, or lives there without a common household with the other parent, the employee must answer whether they mainly (more than 50%) provide for the child's maintenance (yes/no). Grouping of civil statuses per assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert.

examples.name: Married, in household, common household: nothing more asked
Single, in household, common household: contributor asked
In household, no common household: maintenance asked
Not in household: maintenance asked, common household not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Per-child result for an adult child in first education
acceptance_criteria.given: a completed block for an adult child in first education
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the per-child result
acceptance_criteria.then: in the household with a common household: counted for married employees and registered partners; for the single group counted with tariff H if the employee is the main contributor, otherwise not counted. In the household without a common household: with more than 50% maintenance counted (with H for the single group), otherwise not counted. Not in the household: counted with more than 50% maintenance, otherwise not counted, for both groups. Observed calculator results win (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert); inferred results are compared with the calculator before go-live (D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage).

stories.title: Child digit of the tariff code and go-live check of the child paths
stories.i_want: Lonio to turn the per-child results into the child digit of the tariff code, and the child paths not yet observed in the calculator to be checked before go-live
stories.so_that: I no longer click through the calculator per child and can rely on the computed tariff code
stories.priority_reason: Lonio replaces HR's manual calculator step (D-001); unverified paths are a go-live condition (D-009).

acceptance_criteria.title: Child digit is the number of counted children
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee for whom a tariff code is computed
acceptance_criteria.then: the digit is the number of children whose result is 'counted' or 'counted with H', added up over all child blocks (for example three counted children give C3Y); a 'not counted' child adds nothing; without children the digit is 0. There is no maximum number of children (assumption D-044, to be verified by a domain expert); results with more than 3 children are checked against the calculator before go-live (D-009, see OQ-calculator-coverage). Each example below shows one child block.

examples.name: No children
One counted child (married, sole custody)
One child counted with H (single, sole custody)
Child not counted (neither minor nor in first education)

acceptance_criteria.title: Counted with H leads to tariff H for the single group
acceptance_criteria.given: a single, divorced, separated or widowed employee subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: at least one child block has the result 'counted with H'
acceptance_criteria.then: the tariff letter becomes H (the tariff letter itself is decided by the tariff letter rule); for married employees and registered partners no child result is 'counted with H'.

acceptance_criteria.title: Child results are always derived from the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.when: a child answer or an answer it depends on (such as civil status) is changed later by HR
acceptance_criteria.then: the per-child results and the child digit are derived again from the latest answers; the employee cannot change them after submission.

acceptance_criteria.title: Go-live check of the inferred child paths
acceptance_criteria.given: per-child results that are marked inferred (not observed in the calculator) and families with more than 3 children
acceptance_criteria.then: a domain expert compares Lonio's results for these paths with the Zurich calculator before release; observed calculator results always win over the general rule (assumption D-046, to be verified by a domain expert). This is a non-blocking go-live condition, see OQ-calculator-coverage.
